en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
Ārāmavagga 56.
The Training Rule on a Monastery Without Bhikkhus.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, a number of bhikkhunīs who had completed the rains residence in a village monastery went to Sāvatthī.
Those bhikkhunīs said this to those bhikkhunīs:
“Where, venerable ladies, did you complete the rains residence?”
“Was the exhortation successful?
“No, Noble Lady; there were no monks there, so how could the exhortation have been successful?”
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... they complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
"How can these bhikkhunīs dwell for the rains residence in a monastery where there are no bhikkhus? ...
"Is it true, monks, that bhikkhunīs are dwelling for the rains residence in a monastery where there are no bhikkhus?"
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How can this be, monks? How indeed can bhikkhunīs spend the rains retreat in a residence where no bhikkhus are present?”
“Monks, this does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And thus, monks, should the nuns recite this training rule:
‘If any bhikkhunī should spend the rains residence in a dwelling where no bhikkhus are present, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).’”
"But whichever" means whichever such...
"nun" means... [as before].
...pe... this is the nun intended in this context.
A residence "without monks" is one where it is not possible to go for the purpose of receiving exhortation or for communal living.
If one prepares a lodging with the thought, "I will spend the rains retreat," provides drinking water and water for washing, and sweeps the courtyard, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
At the rising of the sun, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
There is no offense—
When the monks who have entered the rains residence have departed, or have left the order, or have died, or have joined another faction;
or in cases of emergency;
or for one who is insane.
"By one who is a first offender":
thus ends the sixth training rule.
